title: Add Two Numbers Written as Text
statement:
You get two non-negative integers a and b written as strings of decimal digits. They can be thousands of digits long, far beyond what a normal number type holds.

Return their sum, also as a string of digits, with no leading zeros (the sum zero is "0"). Do not convert the whole strings to numbers or use a big-integer type: add them digit by digit, the way you would on paper.

examples.why: The carry runs through every digit and still leaves a 1 at the end. Forgetting that final carry gives "000".
Zero plus zero is a single "0", not an empty string.

constraints: a and b contain only digits
Neither has a leading zero unless it is exactly "0"
hints: How do you add two long numbers on paper? Where do you start?
Walk both strings from their last character. Add the two digits and the carry; write the last digit of that sum and carry the rest.
A string shorter than the other just contributes 0 once it runs out. After the loop, a leftover carry becomes one more leading digit. Collect digits in an array and reverse once at the end.

explain.intuition:
Schoolbook addition. Line the numbers up on the right, add column by column from the ones digit, and pass a carry of 0 or 1 to the next column. The sum of two digits plus a carry is at most 9 + 9 + 1 = 19, so the carry never exceeds 1.

The only care points are the ends: the shorter number runs out first (treat its missing digits as 0), and a carry left over after the last column becomes a new leading 1. Building the answer by prepending to a string is O(n²) in many languages, so push digits into an array and reverse once.
steps: Set i and j to the last index of a and b, and carry = 0.
While i ≥ 0, j ≥ 0 or carry > 0: take the digit at each index (0 if it is out of range) and add them with carry.
Push sum % 10 to the output and set carry = Math.floor(sum / 10). Move both indexes left.
Reverse the output and join it.
pitfalls: Dropping the last carry: "999" + "1" must give "1000".
Using Number(a) + Number(b). It loses precision past 2⁵³, which is only 16 digits.
Building the result with digit + result in a loop, which copies the string every time.

solutions.title: Pad, then add column by column
solutions.idea: Left-pad the shorter string with zeros so both have the same length, then add from right to left.

solutions.title: Two pointers from the right
solutions.idea: Walk both strings from the end at once. A pointer that runs off the front contributes 0; the loop also runs while a carry is left.

followups: Subtract instead: return a − b as text, where a ≥ b. What replaces the carry?
Add many numbers at once. Can you do it in one pass over the columns?
